status: authored 2026-10-02, not yet applied to any world
built_by: tools/frostpeak_camp.py build -> build/datapacks/cobblers_frostpeak_camp; audited by tools/frostpeak_camp_audit.py
owner_request: "i feel like a research site around 2079 115 1048 could be cool. i assume we will have a legendary at teh top of the mountain or close by they are looking into. it would be frostpeak shrine yeah." Then: "i got my x or y wrong, the research site is meant to be at the foot of the south end of the frostpeak". The site (688, 688) was measured and accepted on 2026-10-01.
purpose: A small field camp at Frostpeak's south foot whose researchers study Articuno. Its job in the world: the adopted Articuno shrine (data/adopted_legendary_sites.json adopted_articuno_shrine) has no finder, so the camp is how a player learns where to look - a telescope trained on the tower's crown, which shows over the false crest from the summit where the tower stands (moved there 2026-10-02 on the owner's word), field notes on a board, and researchers who point up the mountain. Nothing here promises the shrine's altar works (adopted_legendary_sites.json a_dead_altar_must_not_block; EXP-048): the researchers observe and speculate, and no step, reward or gate requires the altar.
ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/frostpeak_camp.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y. Each piece is seated on max(ground under its footprint) + 1, with a foundation down to the ground under any lower column (tools/shrines.py's convention).

site.measured: 2026-10-02 from tools/ground.py: ground y108..113 over x688..727 z688..727, median 111 rounded (raw median 110.62, relief 4.93); the north edge is the high side (y113), the south-east the low (y109). Nothing any built pack writes and no data point lies within 64 blocks (scanned 2026-10-02 against the full checkout's build/datapacks).

shrine.source: data/adopted_legendary_sites.json sites[id=adopted_articuno_shrine]: placement.centre (x, z) and placement.top_y
shrine.aim: the middle of the part of the tower's centre column visible over the false crest from the telescope (its crown), computed from the heightmap

summit.source: data/towns.json towns[id=frostpeak_shrine].centre: the centre of the pressed summit platform (data/sculpt.json pads frostpeak_shrine, radius 55, y310)
summit.aim: the crest that hides it: the highest elevation angle along the summit's bearing, computed from the heightmap. The summit platform itself is not visible from the camp.

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only, none a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json (white and red wool are not; grey, light grey, orange and the other coloured wools are). No chests: tools/portals_audit.py records a chest as a Gimmighoul spawn condition, though data/spawn_blocks.json does not list it, so barrels carry the stores. No beds: a bed sets a respawn point, which the blackout recovery owns (docs/mechanics/BLACKOUT_RECOVERY_COUPLING.md).
blocks.display_note: the instrument tubes are block_display entities (the format tools/rift_skin.py already uses), not blocks: a block cannot point at an arbitrary bearing. An entity is erased by an export like an NPC, so the instruments function re-summons them.

pieces.why: a plank deck on the high north edge of the bench, the camp's best view of the mountain
the survey's telescope, trained on the crown of the Articuno tower on the summit, the part that shows over the false crest
the surveyor's theodolite, laid on the summit's bearing and stopped at the false crest that hides it
the field notes, on the deck's south edge where a player walking up from the camp reads them first
the mess: a long tent with a smoker, stores and a counter, its door to the fire
sleeping tent, door towards the fire; bedrolls, not beds
the camp's fire between the tents, with log benches; its smoke is the camp's mark from the slopes
crates and barrels hauled up from the coast
a mast with a lantern and a cauldron for a snow gauge (a cauldron fills with powder snow in a cold biome)

researchers.name: Dr. Signe Halvard
researchers.greeting: Mind the tripod. We are the Frostpeak survey: three of us, one telescope, and a tower on the summit that nobody alive remembers being built.

topics.says: That tower, up on the summit. Bearing {shrine_bearing}, just west of north, about {shrine_range} blocks off and far above us. Look where the telescope points: the top {crown_showing} blocks of it stand over the crest. The rest is hidden behind the mountain.
Three winters of notes. Frost on the tower when the slopes are bare, a cold wind out of a clear sky, a pale blue shape the herders swear to. I have not seen it myself. I would very much like to.
There is an old altar in it. Some say it calls the bird; some say it never did. We have not made it do anything, and I would not promise you that anyone can. We watch, and we write down what we see.

Up. North, a touch west, and keep climbing. The summit rises about {climb} blocks above this camp, and past that false crest the top is a flat table of snow with the tower in the middle of it. Once you are over the crest you cannot miss it.

researchers.name: Edda Krell
researchers.greeting: The summit? Not from here. That edge up there is a false crest. The middle of the summit table is another {summit_beyond} blocks behind it, flat as a floor. All you see of it from here is the tower's crown.

topics.says: A theodolite. Two sightings on the board: the crest, bearing {summit_bearing}, and the tower's crown, bearing {shrine_bearing}. Near enough one line: the tower stands on the summit table, behind the crest. That is how we know where the table is without seeing it.
The mountain is. The wild Pokemon on these slopes are not the lowlands' kind, and the weather turns in an hour. Go up with a team you trust and come back down before dark.

researchers.name: Bram Ostrow
researchers.greeting: Close the flap, you are letting the warm out. The soup is for the survey, but sit a minute.

topics.ask: What do you think is up there?
topics.says: The Doctor says a bird. Edda says a surveying problem. I say nobody hauls stone up a mountain for nothing. Whether anything up there still listens, none of us knows.
Frost on the inside of the tent in summer. Snorunt in the supply crates. And once a shadow crossing the summit with no cloud to throw it. Make of that what you like.

spawns.why: Frostpeak already carries 21 surface entries in data/spawns.json (scope frostpeak, level 25-45: Delibird, Crabrawler, Sneasel, Snorunt, Absol, Drampa and their lines; docs/story/ENCOUNTERS.md), which cover the bench. A camp-specific table would add a second author for the same ground for no new species.

item_economy.status: A POINTER, NOT AN ECONOMY (2026-10-02). The owner, verbatim: "the feathers handed out through the research station's dialogue, gated on gym8_cleared". Shrew Station is the one source of lumymon:thunder_feather, lumymon:ember_feather and lumymon:glacier_feather: data/research_station.json economy (the_one_source_2026_10_02, items), built by tools/research_station.py. This camp authors no item and tools/frostpeak_camp.py emits none.
item_economy.the_camps_part: Dr. Halvard's instrument deck (pieces frostpeak_camp_instrument_deck) is the far end of the station's glacier courier errand: the field officer's calibrated spyglass, held out on her deck, is swapped for her season's notes by an advancement the station's pack ships (data/research_station.json economy.courier, tools/research_station.py courier_box reads the deck from this file). Her own conversation stays talk-only; moving the hand-over into it is this file's owner's (a second pass).
item_economy.second_author_resolved_2026_10_02: the question superseded_item_economy.second_author_2026_10_02 left open is answered by the owner's decision in status: one source, the station
item_economy.kubfus_scrolls: NOT the station's and not this camp's: the starter build owns them (docs/mechanics/NATIVE_STARTERS_COST.md section 7.5). Their record is kept in superseded_item_economy.items[0].

superseded_item_economy.superseded_by: item_economy.status, above: the owner's decision of 2026-10-02 that the feathers come from the research station's dialogue. Kept in place as the camp's record of the decisions it carried (the mechanism, the gate and why), which the station's economy now implements
superseded_item_economy.status: DECIDED IN PRINCIPLE, NOT BUILT (2026-10-02). Nothing here is emitted by tools/frostpeak_camp.py; the researchers are still talk-only.
superseded_item_economy.second_author_2026_10_02: OPEN, FOR THE OWNER. A parallel session built the same items into Shrew Station (data/research_station.json economy.items: thunder, ember and glacier feathers from its Director after an errand, the glacier errand running through Dr. Halvard's deck here; Kubfu's scrolls nowhere yet). Both are inert: the station's economy.issuing is false and this economy is not built, so no player can get a feather from either today. One source must be chosen before either is switched on. NATIVE_STARTERS_COST.md 7.5's 'the research station ... needs a reason to exist beyond the shrine' describes Shrew Station (it holds the Eon shrine), so Kubfu's scrolls are likely the station's; the feathers' 'research camp' wording is the owner's own (adopted_legendary_sites.json owner_decisions_2026_10_02.the_three_feathers).
superseded_item_economy.why_here: the owner, 2026-10-02: the research station 'is the place that studies these things' (docs/mechanics/NATIVE_STARTERS_COST.md section 7.5) and 'the place that would produce' the feathers.
superseded_item_economy.mechanism: DECIDED, the owner 2026-10-02: THROUGH DIALOGUE, as a reward for work the researchers ask for, not a shop. 'They are studying the birds, so earning one should mean helping them study.' What the work is (observations, a sighting, samples) is for the dialogue author. No recipe or loot table in the installed pack produces these items (docs/research/notes/legendary-catalogue-reopened.md section 2), so the camp's dialogue is their only source.
